response: Yes, partial expander deflation may exacerbate the adverse effects of radiotherapy in two-stage breast reconstruction. According to the available data, expander deflation immediately prior to radiotherapy may augment the adverse effects, especially in the lower expander pole, possibly due to enhanced radiosensitization resulting from a relative increase in blood flow and tissue oxygenation. This suggests that partial expander deflation can worsen the negative outcomes associated with radiotherapy in two-stage breast reconstruction.
